metadata.what: Three GR00T checkpoints, each trained on a different split, facing the same held-out scenes in the same simulator.
the_axis: varies=policy. Every other plane is single-valued and therefore held,
which is what makes a difference in success rate attributable to the
checkpoint rather than to the world or the scenes.
The compare module declares holds=(evaluation, embodiment) — the mirror
image — so the framework checks from provenance that they really were.
each_checkpoint_is_served_separately: One port per checkpoint, because a GR00T server holds one model. The
policy plane is a socket, so three cohorts is three addresses.
one_gpu_caveat: Three ports is the correct declaration and needs three servers live at once.
A 22 GB L4 holds one GR00T at a time, so on this box the same experiment runs
as three single-cohort passes against one port, and the three run records are
compared afterwards. The manifest is unchanged for a machine that can host all
three; what differs is scheduling, not the experiment.
Pointing all three cohorts at ONE port would be the dangerous shortcut: three
measurements of whichever model happens to be loaded, labelled as three
checkpoints. compare's same_policy note catches it, because all three cohorts
would report an identical policy ref.
